turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Morning. You're a bit early, the doctor's still busy. I'll take your blood pressure while you wait.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, whatever. This is a fuss over nothing.

[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): One forty eight over eighty six. Pulse seventy eight, regular. Your daughter phoned the desk as well. She says one morning last week you were confused, couldn't find the kettle, talking all over the show.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Eish. I was half asleep. I was not confused. She dramatises everything.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come in. Sit. What's the problem today?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): My daughter made the booking. She fusses. I told her it's nothing.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): What is the nothing?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): In the mornings I get a bit clammy, sweaty, and my hands go shaky. Before I eat. It's minor.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. A few weeks. Maybe a month. I don't count.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Every morning?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Most mornings, ja. Not if I sleep late and I actually eat. So, nothing really.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not dizzy.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any cough, tight chest, or short of breath?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of that.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you lost any weight?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Mmm. Hard to say. Maybe. The trousers still fit, so no, not really. I don't know.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): You're diabetic. Still on the tablets?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. The gliklazide and the metforman.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Gliclazide, what dose?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Eighty milligram. One tablet in the morning when I get up.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): With food?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): With rooibos. I skip breakfast. Porridge sits too heavy, so I eat later, a pie at the shop.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Metformin, dose and how often?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Five hundred milligrams, twice a day. Morning, and with supper. I do eat supper, so that one I don't miss.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any other medicines?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Vitamins from the chemist, sitting in the cupboard. I never take them.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Last blood test, what did they tell you?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): At the day hospital, a good while back. They said the H B A one C was borderline. I don't remember a number, I threw the paper out. So I'm fine, hey.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long diabetic?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Twelve years, about. From when I retired off the railways.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Living alone?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Flat in the complex. My girl is in Alberton, she pitches up uninvited. Load shedding killed the gate motor last week, that's the actual problem.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): When the sweats come, hungry or just shaky?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Hungry, not really. Shaky, and sweaty on the chest and the back of the neck. Tea and a biscuit, I sit, it eases.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Blacked out?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): She reported confusion. Did that happen?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag no. I found the kettle, I was just tired and slow. Not confused. I'm seventy two, not ninety.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pouring the tea, hands steady?

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, well, actually, no. The kitchen goes swimmy and I grab the counter, the cup spills. So ja, dizzy, a little, seconds only, and something sweet and it's gone. I didn't reckon that counted.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): It counts. Arms forward, steady now, skin dry and not clammy. Pulse regular, no extra beats. Chest clear.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Morning sweats and the shakes, on gliclazide, no breakfast. Sounds like a low blood sugar. Working idea only, not confirmed.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Low sugar. Ag, I doubt it. I feel lekker right now.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Doses stay as they are. Gliclazide eighty milligrams every morning, metformin five hundred twice a day. Eat something proper before the gliclazide, not just the rooibos.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): If you get shaky, take sugar or juice, sit, and don't drive until it has settled.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bloods are booked. HbA1c, a glucose, and kidney function because of the metformin. Come back in two weeks for the results, that visit is booked as well.
[SEG0051] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sharp. I'll put the bloods on for Thursday morning at the lab, and the review in two weeks.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Thursday for the bloods, review in two weeks.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. She's still making a big thing of a small thing.

spec.situation: Older diabetic on gliclazide and metformin with morning sweating and shakiness; skips breakfast; daughter reports confusion once; doctor reviews doses and plans a blood test.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

bad.reason: Reported by staff via daughter and disputed, but not supported as resolved confusion.
bad.text: Confusion (category=neurological, status=resolved, frequency=once, temporality=past, reported_by=clinical_staff, certainty=disputed)

bad.reason: Diabetes and 12-year duration supported, but duration was reported by patient, not doctor.
Planned Thursday morning supported, but suspected low blood sugar indication for all tests not explicitly stated.
bad.text: HbA1c, glucose and renal function tests (type=laboratory, status=planned, requested_by=doctor, indication=suspected low blood sugar and metformin use, scheduled_datetime=Thursday morning)

omissions.text: Patient initially denied dizziness ('No. Not dizzy.') but later clarified brief dizziness/'kitchen goes swimmy' for seconds while pouring tea, needing to grab the counter and with cup spilling; this contradiction is not captured as a disputed/updated symptom history.
Gliclazide is taken when he gets up and effectively without food/with only rooibos because he skips breakfast.
Metformin timing detail: 500 mg in the morning and with supper; patient says he does eat supper and does not miss that dose.
Pulse was documented as regular in the vital signs measurement.
Patient denied weight loss only equivocally ('Maybe... not really. I don't know'), so recording a definite absence would be inaccurate; weight loss inquiry was uncertain rather than clearly negative.
No other medicines besides diabetes tablets; vitamins from the chemist are present but he never takes them.
Last prior blood test was at the day hospital 'a good while back'; patient recalls being told HbA1c was 'borderline' but does not know the number.
Physical exam included skin dry/not clammy.
Doctor explicitly advised that gliclazide and metformin doses should stay unchanged.
Follow-up logistics were more specific: blood tests scheduled for Thursday morning at the lab, then review in two weeks.
